During the [[22 BBY/Legends|early]] [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[mutant]] [[Geneticist/Legends|genetic]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] '''Zeta Magnus''' created a '''clone army''' from the genetic [[Clone template/Legends|template]] of a [[Thyrsian]] [[Sun Guard]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] named [[Sarsius Torne]]. Inside the throne room of his [[Rennek palace]] in his [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] kingdom known as the [[Dark Worlds]], [[Zeta Magnus]] stored hundreds of [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] in [[Suspended animation/Legends|suspended animation]] in [[Cloning tank|clone cylinders]]. Four of the Sun Guard clones were hand-trained by their prime clone Sarsius Torne and were organized into a [[Squad/Legends|unit]] named [[Tark Squad]]. When a [[Zeta Magnus (clone)|clone]] of Zeta Magnus subjugated the planet [[Skye/Legends|Skye]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] helped disguise Tark Squad as [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] and planted them on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. They were then assigned to accompany a [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] strike force sent to the planet Skye to [[Battle of Skye|arrest]] Zeta Magnus. When the Jedi reached Magnus's [[Kharys' fortress|fortress]], their clones [[Stun/Legends|stunned]] them and brought them before Magnus. The Jedi were eventually able to break free and kill both Tark Squad and the clone of Zeta Magnus. Despite the eradication of Tark Squad, the rest of Zeta Magnus's clone army remained safely hidden in the Unknown Regions.<ref name="swcw" /> 

Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], [[NewsNet]] [[Journalist/Legends|reporter]] [[Andor Javin]] of [[TriNebulon News/Legends|TriNebulon News]] identified [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Cronal|Lord Shadowspawn]] as K'am'ir Zaarin, an alias of Zeta Magnus. Javin claimed that he was in possession of a clone army and was in league with a clone of [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Grand Moff Tarkin]].<ref name="DOAE3">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-3|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 3|nolive=1}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Clone_Warrior.jpg|thumb|left|Atha Prime's clone warriors.]]
[[Atha Prime/Legends|Atha Prime]] was the primary antagonist of the cancelled ''[[The Epic Continues]]'' storyline developed by [[Kenner Products]]. Described as a "genetic master" and the "architect of the Clone Wars", Atha Prime created an army of [[Clone Warrior|clone warriors]] that he used to take over the shattered [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|remnants]] of the post-Endor Empire and to conquer worlds recently liberated by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="G2">{{GalaxyCite|2|Galactic Bazaar|Galactic Bazaar: Tales of Phantom Toys}}</ref> In a cancelled article on Imperial Warlords that was intended to be published in ''[[Polyhedron]]'' magazine, co-author [[Abel G. Peña]] attempted to canonize Atha Prime by consolidating him with the character Shadowspawn first mentioned in the ''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''.<ref name="JC2">{{JCFCite|url=posts/26306274|board=Authors and Artists|thread=The Official Abel G. Pena Discussion Thread|user=Halagad_Ventor|date=2007-04-22|time=8:11 PM}}</ref> When elements of the article were eventually released in the [[2014]] [[StarWars.com]] blog post ''[[The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire]]'', Peña made the first canonical reference to Atha Prime's clone army by describing it as being lead by an [[Arkanian]] geneticist named K'am'ir Zaarin who was in league with Shadowspawn.<ref name="DOAE3" /> In Peña's [[2015]] novella ''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]'', Atha Prime's origins were fleshed out through the character Zeta Magnus, a mutant Arkanian geneticist who used K'am'ir Zaarin as an alias. The novella includes the first appearance of a clone army that Zeta Magnus is creating as a reference to the one lead by Atha Prime.<ref name="swcw" /> It is currently unclear whether Zeta Magnus's Thyrsian clones are visually similar to Atha Prime's clones or whether Zeta Magnus conquered Imperial and Alliance worlds with them as Atha Prime did.
